beforeCompiledNodes.stem: Which additional source-control plan should {patientName}'s hospital team arrange after this CT?

answerChoices.label: Thoracic surgical drainage of the mediastinal collection
answerChoices.rationale: The persistent infected collection lies in the mediastinum and needs additional drainage planning.

answerChoices.label: Pleural catheter drainage of the right hemithorax
answerChoices.rationale: Pleural drainage does not enter the represented mediastinal collection.

answerChoices.label: Repeat drainage of the original cervical cavity
answerChoices.rationale: The original cavity is collapsed while the inferior collection persists.

beforeCompiledNodes.explanation: The new collection is separate from the collapsed cervical cavity and from the pleura. Arrange multidisciplinary mediastinal source control while antibiotics continue. The exact access route depends on full extent and specialist assessment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which imaging study should be requested next to assess {patientName}'s neck mass?

answerChoices.label: Contrast-enhanced CT of the neck
answerChoices.rationale: Cross-sectional contrast imaging assesses the deep extent not shown by ultrasound.

answerChoices.label: Repeat ultrasound of the neck
answerChoices.rationale: Repeating the superficial window may leave the retroclavicular extent unresolved.

answerChoices.label: FDG PET-CT of the body
answerChoices.rationale: Metabolic staging does not replace the dedicated local anatomical assessment needed here.

decisionNodes.explanation: Persistent unexplained adenopathy warrants evaluation. Dedicated contrast CT is the best offered study for the incompletely visualized deep extent; MRI could be appropriate in another offered set.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The contrast CT shows the mass at the left jugular nodal chain, with a fluid-containing center and an enhancing tissue portion along its wall. A cervical portion lies beneath the skin, with extension behind the clavicle. The thyroid and salivary glands are separate; the lesion has no continuity with a major vessel.
decisionNodes.stem: Which initial tissue procedure should {patientName}'s team request for the imaged neck mass?

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided FNA of the tissue component
answerChoices.rationale: Targeted FNA samples the represented tissue rather than treating cyst contents as the whole lesion.

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided FNA of the fluid component
answerChoices.rationale: Cyst contents may not represent the underlying lesional tissue.

answerChoices.label: Open excisional biopsy of the entire neck mass
answerChoices.rationale: An unplanned open diagnostic operation should not replace the initial representative needle approach.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use both technique and target: the best offered initial acquisition is image-guided FNA directed at the tissue component. Fluid contents may not represent the lesion. Selected core sampling can also be appropriate, and is not ranked below FNA in this set.

answerChoices.rationale: Surgical tissue preserves architecture for the unresolved suspected T-cell process.

answerChoices.label: Repeat core biopsy of a cervical node
answerChoices.rationale: Core may suit patients who cannot undergo surgery but does not outrank this represented superficial surgical target after unresolved cores.

answerChoices.rationale: Aspirated cells do not restore the absent nodal architecture.

There is no fever or purulent duct drainage.

decisionNodes.stem: Which intervention should be recommended next for {patientName}'s submandibular duct stone?

answerChoices.label: Transoral duct incision and stone extraction
answerChoices.rationale: The reachable fixed distal stone allows a duct approach that preserves the gland.

answerChoices.label: Extracorporeal shock-wave stone fragmentation
answerChoices.rationale: This serves selected stones not directly accessible through a duct approach.

answerChoices.label: Transcervical submandibular gland excision
answerChoices.rationale: Gland removal is disproportionate before addressing this accessible duct stone.

decisionNodes.explanation: Use location and actual access to choose the intervention. Failed basket capture of a fixed distal stone can lead to transoral extraction rather than removal of the whole gland.
sourceLabels: Michael Koch et al. (2021): Treatment of Sialolithiasis: What Has Changed?

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: After transoral stone removal, meal-related swelling and pain stop and clear saliva flows from the duct. Follow-up ultrasound still shows a small calcific focus within an intraparenchymal branch beyond the segment entered at sialendoscopy.
decisionNodes.stem: Which follow-up plan best fits {patientName}'s residual salivary finding?

answerChoices.label: Clinical follow-up for recurrent gland symptoms
answerChoices.rationale: A residual image finding without current symptoms does not itself justify another procedure.

answerChoices.label: Repeat sialendoscopy for residual stone extraction
answerChoices.rationale: Another extraction has no demonstrated symptomatic target here.

answerChoices.label: Elective referral for submandibular gland excision
answerChoices.rationale: Gland removal to clear an asymptomatic image is not supported by this record.

decisionNodes.explanation: Read the residual image alongside current function. Conservative follow-up can be appropriate for an asymptomatic intraparenchymal stone; gland removal is not required to make the image stone-free.

decisionNodes.stem: Which sampling procedure should {patientName}'s team request next for the parotid mass?

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: Core tissue can supply histological relationships unavailable in the viable unresolved cytology.

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound-guided repeat FNA biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: Another cell preparation may remain unable to distinguish these histotypes.

answerChoices.label: Open incisional parotid biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: Opening the intact major gland is generally avoided before suitable needle tissue assessment.

decisionNodes.explanation: The FNA obtained viable lesional cells but did not resolve histotype. A selected core is a supported next acquisition; no fixed number of failed aspirations or universal need for core is asserted.

decisionNodes.stem: Which imaging request best completes local assessment of {patientName}'s parotid cancer?

answerChoices.label: Contrast MRI of the neck and skull base
answerChoices.rationale: MRI supplies preferred local soft-tissue assessment for this malignancy and new nerve findings.

answerChoices.label: Bone-focused CT of the skull base
answerChoices.rationale: Bone-focused CT does not supply the same soft-tissue assessment for the new neurological concern.

answerChoices.label: FDG PET-CT of the body
answerChoices.rationale: Systemic staging cannot replace the specific local question raised by examination.

decisionNodes.explanation: The new weakness and sensory change alter the local extent question. Contrast MRI is the best offered local study; dedicated bone assessment and distant staging answer different questions.

beforeCompiledCases.learningSummary: Parotid malignancy does not itself require nerve sacrifice. Preserve the functioning separable branches while completing tumor resection. Gross invasion of a functioning nerve is a separate withheld boundary. Tumor within small nerve sheaths is perineural growth. It supports postoperative local radiotherapy discussion despite clear resection; it does not prove that the spared main facial nerve should have been removed. Routine cisplatin addition is unsupported.

beforeCompiledCases.presentation: {patientName}, a 68-year-old man, attends clinic after an outside admission for painful right parotid swelling. The founder reviews a point before source control: despite intravenous antibiotics and hydration, fever persisted and mouth opening became more restricted. Ultrasound described superficial gland enlargement, but the deep lobe was hidden by the mandible. At that point he was handling secretions without stridor.

answerChoices.label: Contrast-enhanced CT of the neck
answerChoices.rationale: CT can assess a deep collection and extent hidden from ultrasound.

answerChoices.rationale: The surface window may still leave the mandible-obscured deep compartment unseen.

answerChoices.rationale: Unenhanced CT can show calcification but lacks the enhancement information needed to map complicated soft-tissue infection.

decisionNodes.stem: Which imaging request was appropriate after cervical drainage in {patientName}'s outside deep-neck infection admission?

answerChoices.label: Contrast CT of the neck and chest
answerChoices.rationale: The new thoracic finding requires mapping the cervical source and possible inferior extension.

answerChoices.label: Contrast CT limited to the neck
answerChoices.rationale: A neck-only field can miss the inferior focus suggested by retrosternal pain.

answerChoices.label: CT pulmonary angiography of the chest
answerChoices.rationale: A pulmonary-arterial protocol does not evaluate the entire neck-to-thorax infection pathway.

decisionNodes.explanation: Persistent fever and new retrosternal pain after deep neck infection raise concern for inferior extension even as the neck improves. Contrast neck-and-chest imaging maps the connected compartments.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The contrast CT shows the original cervical cavity collapsed around its drain. A separate rim-enhancing fluid pocket descends into the central chest behind the sternum, between the lungs, below the thoracic inlet. It remains outside both pleural spaces. Intravenous antimicrobial treatment continues.
decisionNodes.stem: Which additional source-control plan should {patientName}'s hospital team arrange after this CT?

answerChoices.label: Thoracic surgical drainage of the mediastinal collection
answerChoices.rationale: The persistent infected collection lies in the mediastinum and needs additional drainage planning.

answerChoices.label: Pleural catheter drainage of the right hemithorax
answerChoices.rationale: Pleural drainage does not enter the represented mediastinal collection.

answerChoices.label: Repeat drainage of the original cervical cavity
answerChoices.rationale: The original cavity is collapsed while the inferior collection persists.

decisionNodes.explanation: The new collection is separate from the collapsed cervical cavity and from the pleura. Arrange multidisciplinary mediastinal source control while antibiotics continue. The exact access route depends on full extent and specialist assessment.
